transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-13
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Carlos Ramirez, Meera Patel, Samir Khan, Ava Liu (Acme)

Summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evals and recent regressions. Focus on prompt set updates, scoring thresholds, and guardrail behavior observed in last run. Agreed next steps: updated prompts, 1k regression test, SOC2 docs, schedule deep-dive on guardrails.

Topics: quality metrics, scoring rubric, quantization regression, prompt-engineering, guardrails/safety filters, action items

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give folks a minute to hop in, but quick agenda - results from the last eval, prompt updates, regressions and next steps.
00:14 Carlos: yep, thanks Jordan, yeah we ran the latest batch yesterday against the 7B quantized and the baseline. we saw a drop in "financial-summarization accuracy" on the regulatory prompts.
00:28 Meera: specifically the coverage on required disclosure sentences fell from about 92% to like 81% on the quantized run, so that's what worried us.
00:42 Priya: (SE) okay thanks for that detail. quick clarification - when you say "quantized run" is that the nvnc q4 run or the int4 experimental?
00:56 Meera: it's the q4_0 compile from the dedicated nodes, the one we ran last Tuesday.
01:10 Priya: got it, okay. so couple things - first we want to confirm if this is a prompt sensitivity issue versus a kernel/decoder difference. we saw similar tokenization shifts in other clients when the KV cache rounding changed.
01:26 Samir: (slight audio) can I interject - from a security side it's also important we verify there's no degradation tied to data retention or prefix caching that could leak PII in summaries.
01:40 Jordan: good point Samir. Lena, i'll capture that as part of the docs pack.
01:45 Lena: yup noted.
01:48 Jordan: Meera, can you walk through one of the failing examples? that will help Priya triage.
01:58 Meera: sure, um example 137 - original doc includes three mandated disclosures, the model omitted the second disclosure or paraphrased it in a way that regulators wouldn't accept. it was subtle but critical.
02:12 Priya: okay i'm thinking two parallel paths - prompt adjustments (explicit anchors for mandatory sentences), and a regression run to see if it's deterministic on the q4 artifact or intermittent.
02:26 Carlos: yeah we need determinism, our compliance team will want a reproducible mitigation plan.
02:34 Priya: for the prompt changes i propose adding a structured template: a required bullet for disclosures and a high-penalty token for omission. also we'll instrument scoring to flag missing sentences as a hard fail in the eval spreadsheet.
02:48 Meera: that makes sense. how will that affect overall fluency? we've been balancing not to over-constrain outputs.
03:00 Priya: good question - initial plan is to use post-generation reranking with a strict matcher for disclosure clauses, not heavy-handed prompt forcing. so the generator stays fluent, reranker enforces mandated parts.
03:16 Jordan: quick note: we did see slight throughput impact with reranking enabled on Dedicated at high QPS, so we should scope latency tradeoffs.
03:28 Carlos: latency is secondary to compliance, but if it's a 30% hit at peak QPS that's concerning for production budget.
03:40 Priya: understood - we'll quantify. one more thing, the golden set scoring - are we still aligned on pass threshold at 0.85 quality score?
03:52 Meera: yes 0.85 is what we discussed, but for regulatory prompts we had suggested raising to 0.9 as a stricter bar.
04:04 Jordan: ok noted. we'll put regulatory prompt family on a 0.9 threshold in the scoring sheet.
04:10 Lena: i'll update the sheet and re-share.
04:16 Jordan: on regressions - Priya, can you explain what logs you'll need from Acme to debug the tokenization vs model variant question.
04:26 Priya: sure - ideally we need the raw request payloads, the model variant identifier (model hash/compilation tag), and a sample of the tokenized input + raw logits for the failing examples. if sharing logits is sensitive we can do a secure session with your infra.
04:44 Samir: happy to do a secure session, but we do need Redwood's assurance on rotation of any shared keys and that logs won't persist longer than necessary.
04:54 Jordan: we'll share our security playbook and SOC2 summary. Lena will send the docs.
05:02 Carlos: switching topics - guardrails. we saw a case where the content filter flagged a customer-facing summary even though it was benign; it looked like a false positive.
05:14 Meera: that one was odd, it happened on the baseline too so maybe it's upstream in the content lexicon.
05:24 Priya: we can tune the lexicon and add a contextual override for finance domain. we also have a mode to surface "ambiguous flags" for manual review instead of blocking.
05:36 Ava: would manual review be viable at our scale? we're processing tens of thousands per day.
05:44 Carlos: not at scale. we need a low-latency deterministic fallback - e.g., route to a higher-trust model variant or call a narrower safety policy, not full human review.
05:56 Priya: agreed - we can implement a routing policy: if flagged but similarity to trusted template > 0.8 then auto-allow, else rerun on higher-trust variant. we'll prototype that.
06:10 Meera: ok, can we see logs for the false positive? i can share the case id.
06:16 Carlos: case id ACME-4423, sent in chat.
06:20 Jordan: perfect.
06:22 (pause, crosstalk)
06:40 Jordan: quick housekeeping - scheduling: next deep dive should be week of 05/19, does that work?
06:48 Meera: yes that works for engineering.
06:52 Samir: security prefers 05/20 in afternoon PST.
06:58 Jordan: noted, we'll propose 05/20 1pm PT.
07:02 Priya: returning to regression tests - i recommend a 1k sample set stratified across templates, regulatory docs, and edge cases Meera flagged. we'll run baseline and q4_0 quantized then produce confusion matrices and per-class recall.
07:18 Meera: that will be helpful. please also include a token-level diff for the cases where disclosures were truncated.
07:26 Priya: yes we'll include token diffs and logits snapshots.
07:30 Carlos: how long will that take to run? we need results before the compliance review on 05/28.
07:36 Priya: timeline - 3 business days to run and analyze once we have the 1k set, so if we get the prompts by 05/15 we can deliver by 05/21.
07:48 Jordan: good.
07:50 (audio glitch)
08:10 Meera: small note on scoring - we discovered a weighting bug in our local eval script where coverage weight wasn't applied for the disclosure family; fixed locally and reran on last week's set. will share updated counts.
08:26 Priya: thanks for catching that, that could explain part of the delta.
08:30 Meera: yeah it bumped some of the baseline scores up by 2-3 points.
08:36 Jordan: great.
08:38 Samir: procurement question - if we move to Dedicated or Private, what are the lock-in and data residency implications?
08:48 Jordan: short answer: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in our cloud region with data isolation; Private gives you customer-controlled VPC or on-prem and full control over KMS. tradeoffs are ops overhead vs compliance.
09:04 Samir: we need an architecture diagram for Private and a list of supported KMS/HSM partners.
09:12 Lena: i'll include that in the docs pack.
09:16 Jordan: also we'll attach a recommended config that minimizes cross-tenant caches and ensures logs are routed to your S3 bucket.
09:24 Carlos: excellent.
09:26 Priya: one more technical detail - we noticed the q4 quantization had different beam/temperature tuning in the compiler; we should align decoding params across variants before comparing. otherwise you're comparing apples and oranges.
09:40 Meera: ah that might be why fluency differed. good catch.
09:44 Priya: i'll export the exact decode params (beam, temp, top_p) used in each run.
09:50 Jordan: ok to summarize - action items and next steps as listed; primary deliverables from Redwood are updated prompt set + scoring sheet (Jordan), regression run results (Priya), SOC2/architecture docs (Lena). Acme will provide failing examples and tokenization traces (Meera/Carlos).
10:06 Carlos: yep that's right.
10:08 Ava: quick ask - can we get a short deck that explains reranking vs prompt forcing, so stakeholders understand the UX tradeoffs?
10:18 Jordan: yes we have a one-pager, will share.
10:22 Meera: also please include cost delta estimates for reranking vs higher-trust variant fallbacks.
10:30 Jordan: noted - we'll add cost per 1k requests assumptions.
10:34 (wrap-up)
10:40 Jordan: thanks everyone - big thanks to Priya for digging in, Lena for docs. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and propose 05/20 for deep dive. any final comments?
10:50 Samir: no, thanks.
10:52 Carlos: good sync.
10:54 Jordan: ok bye all.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and small audio glitches, some technical terms rendered loosely (q4_0, KV cache), natural speech fillers preserved.
